result: The authors designed a target-agnostic workflow to isolate antibodies from a malaria-exposed donor, sorting 1496 IgG+ memory B cells and screening supernatants against gamete/gametocyte lysates. This yielded 14 monoclonal antibodies targeting sexual stage proteins including Pfs230, Pfs48/45, and other unidentified proteins.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly affirm the target-agnostic screening approach as a strength of the manuscript. One reviewer states 'Strengths of the manuscript include the target-agnostic screening approach' and another notes 'The experiments are based on the use of target-agnostic memory B cell sorting and screening approaches.' The methodology and antibody isolation results are not questioned.

result: Seven mAbs exhibited gamete surface binding, with four (B1C5K, B1C5L, B2C10L, B2E9L) showing high binding even at low concentrations and reduced binding to Pfs48/45/Pfs230 knockout gametes. Seven mAbs showed strong transmission-reducing activity (TRA>80%) at 500 µg/ml, though none had substantially higher TRA than previously described antibodies. B1E11K showed distinctive binding patterns recognizing only a fraction of gametes.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these characterization results without challenge. One reviewer explicitly notes 'The antibodies displayed a range of transmission-reducing activities and recognized different Pf sexual stage proteins. However, none of these antibodies had substantially higher TRA than previously described antibodies,' acknowledging the findings while noting their limitations. The gamete binding and TRA data are treated as valid experimental observations.

result: Western blot and ELISA experiments identified B1C5K and B1C5L as targeting Pfs48/45 domain 2, B2C10L as recognizing Pfs230 (though not the Pfs230CMB construct), and B1E11K as binding to unprocessed Pfs230 plus several unidentified proteins ranging from 70-250 kDa.
evaluation: Reviewers describe the characterization methods as 'highly appropriate' and note the authors 'have built a compelling case' through 'Western blotting of recombinant proteins to native parasite material, use of knockout lines to validate specificity.' The antigen identification results are accepted as part of the thorough characterization without specific critique.

result: B1E11K was shown to be cross-reactive to multiple proteins containing glutamate-rich repeats following an 'EE-XX-EE' pattern, including Pfs230, Pf11.1, RESA, RESA3, and LSA3. Protein microarray, mass spectrometry, and western blot confirmed binding to these antigens, with B1E11K exhibiting highest specificity for RESA-derived peptides (EC50 at least 100-fold greater than other glutamate-rich peptides).
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm this cross-reactivity finding as a major contribution. One states 'The authors present compelling evidence that one antibody, B1E11K, is cross-reactive with multiple proteins containing glutamate-rich repeats.' Another notes 'The demonstration that B1E11K is cross-reactive to multiple proteins containing glutamate-rich repeats...should be of interest to many in the field.' The evidence from multiple orthogonal methods is described as 'compelling.'

result: Epitope mapping showed B1E11K binds a minimal 10AA RESA epitope, with binding stoichiometry experiments (ITC, BLI, SEC-MALS, nsEM) demonstrating that two Fab molecules bind to the 16AA RESA P2 peptide in a 2:1 Fab:peptide complex with approximately six-fold difference in affinity between 10AA (KD=484 nM) and 16AA (KD=74 nM) peptides.
evaluation: Reviewers describe the biophysical characterization as 'impressive' and 'highly appropriate,' noting 'An impressive set of biophysical experiments were performed to extensively characterize the interactions of B1E11K with various repeat motifs and lengths.' The stoichiometry and binding data from ITC, peptide mapping, SEC-MALS, and negative stain EM are accepted without critique as part of the thorough characterization.

result: A 2.6 Å crystal structure revealed two B1E11K Fabs binding to the RESA P2 peptide in a head-to-head conformation with affinity-matured homotypic interactions through two interfaces. The paratope is enriched in arginine and histidine residues forming salt bridges with glutamate residues and hydrogen bonds with asparagine residues of RESA repeats, explaining the higher specificity for RESA. Multiple residues in the homotypic interface underwent somatic hypermutation.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly highlight the structural findings as a major contribution. One states 'using X-ray crystallography they show that two B1E11K Fabs bind to a 16 aa RESA repeat in a head-to-head conformation using homotypic interactions and provide a separate example from CSP, of affinity-matured homotypic interactions.' Another notes 'Excitingly, the structure revealed that two Fabs bound simultaneously to the peptide and made homotypic antibody-antibody contacts. This had only previously been observed before with antibodies directed against CSP repeats.' The structural data are treated as compelling evidence.

result: B1E11K represents a novel example of homotypic antibody interactions extending beyond CSP to other Plasmodium proteins with glutamate-rich repeats expressed across various life cycle stages, demonstrating that this mode of recognition is not unique to CSP.
evaluation: All reviewers emphasize this as a key finding and novel insight. One states 'this mode of recognition of Pf proteins, previously described only for Pf circumsporozoite protein (PfCSP), extends to other repeats expressed across various stages' and notes it provides 'new insights into humoral immune responses.' Another reviewer states this finding 'should be of interest to many in the field,' indicating acceptance of the broader significance of extending homotypic interactions beyond CSP.

result: Despite recognizing multiple antigens including sexual stage proteins, mAb B1E11K did not show transmission-reducing activity (TRA) in standard membrane feeding assays.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this finding without challenge. One reviewer notes the authors appropriately caveat their discussion by stating 'although we note that mAb B1E11K isolated and characterized in this study did not show TRA.' The lack of TRA is accepted as a valid experimental observation that does not diminish the structural and immunological insights provided by B1E11K characterization.
